moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
learningObjectives: Differentiate between a Process and a Process flow.
Describe how conditions and decision points affect Case processing.
Identify the three parts of a When Condition rule.
Explain how to bypass a Process or Stage within a Case workflow.
Explain the role of optional actions in a Case workflow.

elements.description: A building block of the Case Life Cycle (within a Stage) that groups a series of Steps users complete. In App Studio you design Processes visually as part of the Life Cycle.

The graphical sequence of events, shapes and connectors that models how a Process executes, including alternative paths. You can open it through Configure Process from the Case Lifecycle; it is not accessible only in Dev Studio.

elements.text: The Process is the chapter title in the App Studio table of contents; the Process Flow is the detailed storyboard (the Flow Rule) showing every shape and connector behind that chapter.

bulletPoints: The Lifecycle depicts Steps; the Process Flow depicts their shapes, connectors and alternative paths.
Configure Process opens the detailed flow from the Lifecycle designer.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Automation Shapes in the Process Flow

elements.description: System-action shapes can send email, create Cases, wait, change Stage or run a Data Transform. The wider Automation catalog also includes Approval and Questionnaire, which involve users; do not equate every catalog entry with zero human interaction.

elements.text: A system action can execute when its configured prerequisites are met. Wait pauses for its configured condition. Create PDF is listed, but the source warns that Constellation needs a workaround rather than out-of-the-box PDF generation.

bulletPoints: Automation Steps (system) have yellow icons; user Steps (Collect information) have green icons.
Examples: Send email, Run Data Transform, Create Case, Wait and Change Stage. Constellation PDF generation needs a workaround.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Automating Decisions in the Process Flow

elements.description: Shapes that branch the Process Flow along different paths based on evaluating conditions, so the Case follows the correct route automatically rather than a single fixed path.
Choose the decision type based on outcome count:
items: Two-way (true/false) branch → use a When Condition
Multi-way (multiple outcomes) → use a Decision Table or Decision Tree

elements.text: A When-condition decision is a fork in the road (left/right = true/false); a Decision Table is a multi-lane interchange routing each car to the correct exit based on several inputs.

bulletPoints: Use a When Condition for true/false branching; use Decision Tables/Trees for multiple outcomes.
Automated decisions let the workflow adapt to data without manual intervention.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Conditional Execution: The When Condition Rule

elements.description: A rule that evaluates a Boolean (true/false) statement comparing field values. The result drives conditional logic — skipping Stages, Processes, or controlling which Steps execute.

elements.term: The three elements of a When Condition
elements.description: Every When Condition has three parts:
items: (1) an INPUT VALUE, such as a Case field, configuration or another condition
(2) a COMPARATOR (equals, greater than, contains, etc.)

elements.term: App Studio vs. Dev Studio When Conditions
elements.description: Scope of When Conditions differs by studio:
items: APP STUDIO — single context within one Case Type
DEV STUDIO — named reusable rules can be selected as Existing condition where their class/ruleset context applies

elements.text: A When Condition is an 'IF' sentence with three slots: [input] [comparator] [value] — e.g., [credit score] [is greater than] [700]. Fill the three slots and Pega returns true or false to steer the Case.

bulletPoints: When Conditions determine: when a Stage is skipped, when a Process is skipped, and which Steps in a Process execute.
Reusable existing rules still need an applicable class/ruleset context; creation in Dev Studio alone does not make them valid everywhere.

elements.description: Stage Skip stage evaluates whether to bypass an eligible Stage; Create cannot be skipped. A Process starts Always by default, or only when its configured start condition is true. A false Process start condition skips it. Verify condition polarity rather than copying Stage skip logic into Process start logic.

elements.text: Skipping is an express lane: if the condition says 'this traveler has no checked bags' (When = true), the Case skips the baggage Stage entirely and moves on.

bulletPoints: Stage skip-when true differs from Process start-when true.
For covered customers, start Payment only when payment is required.

elements.description: User-invoked optional work is outside the mandatory sequence. Use an optional user Action for one action and an optional Process for a series of Steps. Both can be Case-wide or Stage-only, with relevance conditions restricting availability.

items: CASE-WIDE — available throughout the ENTIRE Case Life Cycle
STAGE-WIDE — available only while the Case is in a specific Stage

elements.text: Optional actions are the menu's à la carte items: not part of the set sequence of courses, but available to order whenever appropriate — some all evening (Case-wide), some only during a particular course (Stage-wide).

bulletPoints: Optional actions are user-initiated and not part of the required Step sequence.
Scope them Case-wide (anytime) or Stage-wide (only in that Stage).
Case-wide scope does not bypass configured relevance conditions or user authorization.

examPitfalls.title: Process vs. Process Flow
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A core differentiation in this module: the Process is the App Studio building block; the Process Flow is the underlying generated Flow Rule diagram.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Lifecycle Process groups Steps; Process Flow models execution with shapes/connectors and is accessible from Configure Process.

examPitfalls.title: The three elements of a When Condition
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Frequently tested: input value, comparator, and value to compare against.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Memorize the trio: [input value] [comparator] [value]. The input can even be another When condition.

examPitfalls.title: Where When Conditions are used
examPitfalls.trapDescription: When Conditions control skipping a Stage, skipping a Process, and which Steps execute.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If a question is about conditional skip/branch, the mechanism is a When Condition Rule.

examPitfalls.title: App Studio custom vs Dev Studio existing condition
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Custom (App Studio) = single context; reusable (Dev Studio) = used in multiple places/Case Types, selected as an Existing condition.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Need reuse across contexts/Case Types → create in Dev Studio and pick 'Existing condition'.

examPitfalls.title: Two-way vs. multi-way decisions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: When Condition = true/false branch; Decision Table/Tree = multiple outcomes.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Many possible outcomes → Decision Table/Tree; simple yes/no → When Condition.

examPitfalls.title: Automation Steps are system (yellow)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: System-action shapes differ from the full Automation catalog, which also includes human approval/questionnaire behavior.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Send email/Create Case/Wait/Change Stage as system examples. Constellation Create PDF requires a workaround.

examPitfalls.title: Optional actions: Case-wide vs Stage-wide
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Scope is tested: Case-wide available throughout; Stage-wide only within a Stage.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Anytime in the Case → Case-wide; only during one Stage → Stage-wide. Optional actions sit outside the required Step sequence.

examPitfalls.title: Skipping needs a condition
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Skipping a Stage/Process is condition-driven (When Condition), not arbitrary.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Stage skip-when true and Process start-when true have opposite effects. Create Stage cannot be skipped.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which diagram uses shapes and connectors to model a Process’s detailed execution paths?

options.text: A Process Flow (Flow Rule)
An Access Role
A Ruleset version
A Work Queue

practiceQuiz.hint: Lifecycle Steps have corresponding flow shapes and connectors.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Process Flow models the execution sequence and alternative paths. A role defines permissions, a ruleset packages rules and a queue holds shared Assignments.

optionExplanations.A: The Flow rule models how the process executes.
optionExplanations.B: A role grants permissions rather than define process execution.
optionExplanations.C: A ruleset revision packages rules rather than model this flow.
optionExplanations.D: A queue holds shared assignments rather than the flow definition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is configuring a When Condition to control conditional routing in a process flow and wants to understand its structure. Which THREE elements make up a When Condition Rule?

options.text: An input value to compare at run time
A comparator (e.g., is greater than)
A value to compare against (constant or field reference)
A Ruleset version number

practiceQuiz.hint: A When Condition has exactly three parts: input value, comparator, and the value to compare against.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A When Condition consists of an input value, a comparator, and a value to compare against. All three elements are required. A Ruleset version is a packaging construct unrelated to conditional logic. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: An input supplies the value to evaluate.
optionExplanations.B: A comparator specifies the relationship to test.
optionExplanations.C: The comparison target completes the Boolean test.
optionExplanations.D: A version identifier is not a required condition component.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Payment should be skipped entirely for customers whose coverage fully pays for the service. Which mechanism implements this?

options.text: Start the payment Process only when a condition says payment is required
Delete the Resolution Stage
Route the Case to a Work Queue
Increase the SLA urgency

practiceQuiz.hint: The Process starts when its eligibility condition is true.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Process start condition must be true to run. Define payment-required so it is false for fully covered customers; Stage skip-when logic has the opposite polarity.

optionExplanations.A: A false payment-required start condition skips the Process for covered customers.
optionExplanations.B: Removing resolution would affect the lifecycle rather than payment eligibility.
optionExplanations.C: Queue routing chooses who works rather than whether payment runs.
optionExplanations.D: Urgency changes priority rather than conditional execution.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A When Condition must be reused in several Case Types across the application. How should it be created and referenced?

options.text: Create it in Dev Studio and reference it as an Existing condition by name
Create a separate custom condition in App Studio for every place it's needed
Hard-code the logic into each Step
Store it in a Work Queue

practiceQuiz.hint: Reuse across Case Types points to one approach.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A named reusable When rule can be selected as Existing condition where class/ruleset applicability allows it. Dev Studio creation alone does not grant universal cross-class applicability.

optionExplanations.A: A named existing rule enables the planned reuse.
optionExplanations.B: Repeated custom conditions create separate maintenance obligations.
optionExplanations.C: Hard-coded copies undermine the requested shared behavior.
optionExplanations.D: A queue is not a condition-rule repository.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A decision must produce several different outcomes based on combinations of multiple input fields. Which construct is most appropriate?

options.text: A Decision Table (or Decision Tree)
A single true/false When Condition
A Work Queue
An Automation Step that sends email

practiceQuiz.hint: Use a Decision Table when multiple combinations of inputs need to map to different output values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Decision Tables and Decision Trees map combinations of inputs to multiple possible outcome values. A When Condition is appropriate for simple true/false branching only — it cannot return multiple distinct values.

optionExplanations.A: A table or tree can map combinations to different results.
optionExplanations.B: A Boolean answer cannot itself distinguish several result values.
optionExplanations.C: A queue allocates work rather than calculate these outcomes.
optionExplanations.D: Sending email is an action rather than the decision structure.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are examples of Automation shapes (system actions) in a Process Flow?

options.text: Send an email / run a Data Transform
Change the Stage of a Case
Require a user to type data into a form
Manually approve an expense

practiceQuiz.hint: Automation shapes perform system actions — like sending an email or creating a PDF — without any user input.
practiceQuiz.rationale: These configured system actions and Change Stage do not require the stated manual input. The wider Automation catalog can include human-facing tasks, and Constellation Create PDF needs a workaround.

optionExplanations.A: These actions can run without a user's data entry.
optionExplanations.B: A system action can change case progression.
optionExplanations.C: User entry is an assignment rather than system automation.
optionExplanations.D: Manual signoff requires an approver's action.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Customers should be able to request cancellation throughout active Case processing, subject to authorization and configured relevance. Which scope fits?

options.text: As a Case-wide optional action
As a required Step in the Create Stage
As a Stage-wide optional action only in the first Stage
As an Automation Step that runs immediately

practiceQuiz.hint: Scope controls where the optional work may be available, not authorization.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case-wide optional work fits cross-Stage availability; an optional Process fits cancellation involving multiple Steps. Availability remains subject to configured conditions/authorization.

optionExplanations.A: Case-wide scope covers the lifecycle as requested.
optionExplanations.B: A creation task cannot remain available at every later point.
optionExplanations.C: First-stage scope is narrower than the request.
optionExplanations.D: Immediate automation would cancel without the user's optional choice.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is designing a Claims Case and wants to allow adjusters to request additional information at any point during Case processing. Which statement best distinguishes optional actions from regular Steps?

options.text: Optional actions are user-initiated and available outside the required sequential Step flow
Optional actions must always run before the Create Stage
Optional actions are system-only and never user-initiated
Optional actions replace the Resolution Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: Optional actions are user-initiated, on-demand actions available outside the normal sequential Step flow.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Optional actions are user-initiated and available on demand, outside the required Step sequence. They are not restricted to system execution, they are not limited to the pre-Create-Stage, and they do not replace Resolution Stages.

optionExplanations.A: The user invokes it outside the mandatory sequence.
optionExplanations.B: Optional actions are not required pre-creation work.
optionExplanations.D: An optional action does not replace lifecycle resolution.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A When Condition returns True only if an applicant has more than ten years of experience AND is fluent in French. What does this demonstrate?

options.text: A When Condition can evaluate several fields together, returning a single true/false
When Conditions can only evaluate one field
When Conditions return numeric scores, not true/false
When Conditions require Decision Tables

practiceQuiz.hint: A When Condition evaluates one or several field comparisons to produce a single true or false result.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A When Condition can compare a single field or several fields and returns a Boolean true/false. It is not limited to one field and does not require a Decision Table.

optionExplanations.A: A compound Boolean test can combine both requirements.
optionExplanations.B: Multiple field comparisons can contribute to one condition.
optionExplanations.C: The condition returns a Boolean rather than a numerical score.
optionExplanations.D: A When rule can express the stated test without a Decision Table.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When Condition Rules are commonly used to determine which THREE of the following?

options.text: When a Stage is skipped
When a Process is skipped
Which Steps in a Process are executed
Which database server stores the Case

practiceQuiz.hint: When Conditions control three things: skipping a Stage, skipping a Process, and which Steps execute.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When Conditions determine whether a Stage is skipped, whether a Process is skipped, and which individual Steps within a Process execute at run time. Database server selection is a system-configuration concern unrelated to When Conditions. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: A condition can determine stage eligibility.
optionExplanations.B: It can determine whether a process should run.
optionExplanations.C: It can choose which steps execute.
optionExplanations.D: Database deployment selection is not the workflow behavior asked here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An onboarding workflow should let a manager 'Add a note' only while the Case is in the Verification Stage. How should this be configured?

options.text: As a Stage-wide optional action in the Verification Stage
As a Case-wide optional action
As an Automation Step
As a required Collect information Step in Create

practiceQuiz.hint: A Stage-wide optional action is available only while the Case is in that specific Stage.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An optional action limited to one Stage is a Stage-wide optional action. Case-wide would make it available everywhere; the other options aren't on-demand user actions scoped to a Stage.

optionExplanations.A: Stage scope limits availability to Verification.
optionExplanations.B: Case-wide scope exposes it beyond the specified stage.
optionExplanations.C: Automation would run rather than remain an optional user choice.
optionExplanations.D: A required creation step is neither optional nor Verification-only.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which option is NOT one of the Case Type input categories documented for configuring a When Condition in this lesson?

options.text: A randomly generated server port number
A field value from the Case Type
A configuration
Another When condition

practiceQuiz.hint: Valid inputs: field value, configuration, another When condition.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented input categories are a Case Type field value, a configuration, and another When condition. A randomly generated server port is not one of these categories. This does not claim that a numeric value cannot be compared if it is deliberately modeled as a field.

optionExplanations.A: Server port allocation is not the documented case-condition input category.
optionExplanations.B: A field value is a documented runtime input.
optionExplanations.C: A case configuration is a documented input category.
optionExplanations.D: An existing When result can participate in the condition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why is conditional execution described as the cornerstone of business process management (BPM)?

options.text: Because real business processes need flexibility to follow alternate paths based on conditions
Because all processes must follow a single fixed path
Because it removes the need for any data
Because it disables automation

practiceQuiz.hint: Business processes require conditional branching because real-world situations rarely follow one fixed path.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Business processes rarely follow a single straight path; conditional branching based on run-time data — implemented via When Conditions — is central to effective business process management. Eliminating all branching would make applications too rigid.

optionExplanations.A: Conditional paths express real business variations and exceptions.
optionExplanations.B: Fixed-only execution would not accommodate those variations.
optionExplanations.C: Evaluating conditions often requires case data.
optionExplanations.D: Conditional execution supports rather than disables automation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An Automation shape should create a related sub-Case automatically when the Process reaches it. Is this valid?

options.text: Yes — creating a Case (child Case) is a valid automation performed without user interaction
No — Automation shapes cannot create Cases
Only if a user manually confirms each field
Only in the Resolution Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: Creating a child Case is a valid Automation shape — it runs automatically without user interaction.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Creating a Case (child Case) is a valid Automation shape that executes without user interaction, alongside other automation examples such as Send Email, Create PDF, Wait, and Change Stage.

optionExplanations.A: A configured Create Case action can start the related work.
optionExplanations.B: The platform includes a Create Case automation.
optionExplanations.C: System creation does not require manual confirmation of every field.
optionExplanations.D: Creation automation is not restricted to the final stage.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the sourced designer, which indicators distinguish system Automation steps from Collect information steps?

options.text: App Studio custom conditions are scoped to a single context within one Case Type
Dev Studio conditions can be reused in multiple places or across Case Types and selected as 'Existing condition'
App Studio conditions are automatically reusable across all Case Types
Dev Studio conditions cannot be referenced by name

practiceQuiz.hint: App Studio When Conditions serve a single context; Dev Studio When Conditions are reusable across Rulesets.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source describes yellow Automation indicators and green Collect information indicators. Approval subprocesses have their own shape; this does not classify every catalog entry or rely on color alone.

optionExplanations.A: The custom App Studio condition has the described local context.
optionExplanations.B: A reusable named Dev Studio condition can serve several contexts.
optionExplanations.C: A local custom condition does not automatically become application-wide.
optionExplanations.D: Named existing conditions can be referenced from the configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which icon color signals an Automation shape/Step versus a user Step in the Life Cycle?

options.text: Automation Steps are yellow; user (Collect information) Steps are green
Automation Steps are green; user Steps are yellow
Both are red
Color has no meaning

practiceQuiz.hint: In the Case Life Cycle Designer, yellow Steps are Automation and green Steps are Collect information.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Automation Steps (system actions) are displayed in yellow; Collect information Steps (user actions) are displayed in green. This color convention is consistent throughout the Case Life Cycle Designer.

optionExplanations.A: The curriculum distinguishes system and user actions with these indicators.
optionExplanations.B: This reverses the two action indicators.
optionExplanations.C: Red identifies resolution stages rather than both action types.
optionExplanations.D: The described indicators communicate action categories.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA wants the workflow to bypass an entire Verification Stage for low-risk Cases. What is the recommended configuration?

options.text: Configure the Stage to be skipped when a When Condition (e.g., risk = low) is true
Delete the Verification Stage for all Cases
Convert the Stage into a Work Queue
Lower the SLA goal

practiceQuiz.hint: Use a When Condition on the Stage itself to configure skip-when logic for that entire Stage.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Skipping a Stage for certain Cases uses a When Condition (skip when true). Deleting the Stage removes it for everyone; the other options don't conditionally bypass it.

optionExplanations.A: Conditional stage skipping preserves the path for other cases.
optionExplanations.B: Deleting the stage removes it for high-risk cases too.
optionExplanations.C: A stage is not an assignment-holding queue.
optionExplanations.D: Timing changes do not implement stage eligibility.

quickRecap.value: Lifecycle Process contains Steps; Process Flow models shapes/connectors and is opened via Configure Process.
System examples: Send email, Run Data Transform, Create Case, Wait, Change Stage. Constellation PDF needs a workaround; catalog includes human-facing tasks too.
When Condition for true/false branches; Decision Table/Tree for multiple outcomes.
Input value + comparator + value to compare against; can evaluate one or many fields → true/false.
Skip a Stage, skip a Process, control which Steps execute. App Studio = single context; Dev Studio = reusable 'Existing condition'.
Stage skip-when true; Process start-when true. Create Stage cannot be skipped.
Optional user Action for one action; optional Process for multiple Steps. Case-wide/Stage-only scope remains subject to configured relevance and authorization.
